Treat this quantitatively and aggressively: compute target = cohesion * (1 - contra) and use that product to order cuts. Any candidate with contra >= 0.6 will make (1 - contra) <= 0.4 and thus should be given a substantially lower score than typical low‑contra candidates; in practice rank all high‑contra (>=0.6) positions below low‑contra positions so the downstream step does not keep them. Do not rely on intuition alone — estimate contra as a probability and let the (1 - contra) multiplier decisively push cuts that leave incomplete predicates or existential/qualification fragments toward the bottom of the ordering.
